title: 名实之辩与共相之争
lead: 同名一样问题：普遍的词对应什么？中国思想把它挂在政治秩序上，希腊思想把它挂在本体论上。
leadEn: One problem, two registrations: what does a general term correspond to? Chinese thought filed it under order, Greek thought under being.
west: 从巴门尼德到亚里士多德，「一」与「多」、「共相」是否独立实在成为形而上学核心；中世纪唯实论与唯名论延续同一战场，现代以自然类与抽象对象重开。
westEn: From Parmenides to Aristotle, the one-over-many and the reality of universals sit at the centre of metaphysics; medieval realism and nominalism continue it, and it reopens today as natural kinds and abstract objects.
east: 孔子「正名」先把名实对应作为政治与伦理条件：名不正则言不顺，事不成。名家（公孙龙「白马非马」、惠施历物十事）推进到逻辑与概念分析，但未获得形而上学的最终地位。
eastEn: Confucius' rectification of names first makes name-thing correspondence a political and ethical condition: if names are not correct, speech is not in order and affairs fail. The School of Names (Gongsun Long's 'a white horse is not a horse', Hui Shi's ten theses) presses into logic and concept-analysis, yet never gains final metaphysical status.
bridge: 名家若继续发展，是否会走向独立的本体论？学界分歧于此。可确定的是：同样的语词—世界张力，一处被处理为「如何治」，一处被处理为「什么在」。
bridgeEn: Would the School of Names, allowed to grow, have produced an autonomous ontology? Scholars divide. What is certain is that the same word-world tension was handled as a problem of ordering, there, and of being, here.

sources.label: 亚里士多德《形而上学》Z 卷

title: 道与逻各斯
lead: 两者都是万物的根据与法则，却对「能否被说清」给出相反的判断。
leadEn: Both name the ground and law of all things—and give opposite verdicts on whether that can be said clearly.
west: 逻各斯自赫拉克利特起即指普遍的理性秩序，可循逻辑与定义陈述；斯多亚把它延展为世界理性，基督教《约翰福音》以「太初有道（logos）」承接，翻译选择本身即一次哲学判断。
westEn: From Heraclitus, logos is a universal rational order statable through logic and definition; the Stoics extend it to world-reason, and the Gospel's 'in the beginning was the Word' inherits it—the translation choice is itself a philosophical verdict.
east: 「道可道，非常道」：作为根源的道对既定命名抵抗；它更像生成与通行的方式，而非可列举的法则集合。故修养路径是「减损」与顺应，不是定义与推演。
eastEn: 'The dao that can be spoken is not the constant dao': as source, the dao resists settled naming; it resembles a way things issue and go rather than a listable set of laws. Cultivation is therefore decrease and attunement, not definition and deduction.
bridge: 差异落在语言能否穷尽实在：逻各斯传统偏向「能」，道传统偏向「有剩余」。这一分歧塑造了各自的论证风格——一边重定义与反驳，一边重譬喻与点拨。
bridgeEn: The difference lies in whether language can exhaust reality: the logos tradition leans yes, the dao tradition leans 'there is a remainder'. It shaped argumentative style—one side prizes definition and refutation, the other analogy and pointer.

sources.label: 赫拉克利特残篇 DK22 B1

title: 仁义与正义、效用
titleEn: Ren and Yi vs Justice and Utility
lead: 面对同一批冲突：如何分配、对谁负责。一端从关系出发，一端从原则出发。
leadEn: Same conflicts, different anchors: how to allocate, to whom one answers. One side starts from relations, the other from principles.
west: 西方规范伦理以可普遍化的原则为第一：康德的义务、密尔的效用、罗尔斯的正义原则，都要求对「任意的人」成立，特殊关系须被原则解释。
westEn: Western normative ethics takes universalisable principles as first: Kant's duty, Mill's utility, Rawls's principles of justice all must hold for persons qua persons, with special relations explained by the principle.
east: 儒家以「仁」为总德、以「义」为处事的宜：爱有差等，从亲亲出发推扩（老吾老以及人之老）。伦理单元是角色中的具体人，故修身先于立法。
eastEn: Confucianism makes benevolence (ren) the sum of virtue and rightness (yi) the fitting response; love has gradations, extended from one's own kin to other people's. The unit is the person-in-relationship, so self-cultivation precedes legislation.
bridge: 墨家「兼爱」恰是儒家的内部反题——近乎无差等的爱，与功利精神高度相似，却在战国后被中断。当代德性伦理与关怀伦理的兴起，使「关系优先」重新获得哲学地位。
bridgeEn: Mohist impartial concern is Confucianism's internal antithesis—near-undifferentiated love, akin in spirit to utilitarianism, yet cut off after the Warring States. The rise of virtue ethics and ethics of care has restored the philosophical standing of relations-first thinking.

sources.label: 《孟子·梁惠王上》
sources.labelEn: Mencius, King Hui of Liang I

title: 天理与自然法
lead: 两种「道德秩序内嵌于宇宙」的学说，一个凭修养体认，一个凭理性发现。
leadEn: Two doctrines that moral order is built into the cosmos: one realised by cultivation, one discovered by reason.
west: 从斯多亚到阿奎那，自然法是理性对永恒法的分有，可通过本性目的推知并用于裁判人定法；近代由格劳秀斯世俗化，成为人权论的祖本。
westEn: From the Stoa to Aquinas, natural law is a rational participation in eternal law, knowable from natural purposes and used to judge positive law; Grotius secularised it, making it the ancestor of rights doctrine.
east: 宋明儒的「天理」既是物之则也是人之则：性即理、心即理两条进路的分歧正在于此理何从而得。人欲之私遮蔽它，故工夫论（格物、主敬、致良知）是认识论也是伦理学。
eastEn: For Neo-Confucians, tianli is at once the norm of things and of persons; the split between 'nature is principle' and 'mind is principle' turns on how this norm is attained. Private desire veils it, so theories of effort—investigating things, reverence, extending innate knowing—are epistemology and ethics at once.
bridge: 共同点是反对价值纯主观；差异在于来源与通道：自然法依赖立法者式的理性结构与法权语汇，天理依赖修养中的体认与「分殊」的情境拿捏。
bridgeEn: They share a rejection of purely subjective value, and differ in source and access route: natural law leans on a legislator-shaped rational structure and legal vocabulary, tianli on realisation in cultivation and the weighing of concrete distinctions.

sources.label: 阿奎那《神学大全》第一集下集 Q94

title: 无为与消极自由
lead: 都把「不被强行摆布」视为核心善，却一个指向治术与心境，一个指向权利边界。
leadEn: Both treat not being forced as the central good—one toward statecraft and states of mind, the other toward the boundary of rights.
west: 消极自由（伯林、贡斯特）问「他人干涉的最小领域在哪里」，答案是制度性的：以权利与限权划出不可侵犯的空间，并可被国家积极保障。
westEn: Negative liberty (Berlin, Constant) asks where the minimal area of non-interference by others lies; the answer is institutional—rights and limited government mark an inviolable space the state itself may guarantee.
east: 无为在治国侧是「治大国若烹小鲜」「我无为而民自化」，在修身侧是不以造作之力扭折事态；它不依赖权利概念，而依赖对「为」之时机与力度的敏感。
eastEn: In governance wuwei is 'ruling a great state as one cooks a small fish' and 'I do nothing and the people transform themselves'; in cultivation it is not straining events out of shape. It needs no rights concept, only sensitivity to the timing and pressure of acting.
bridge: 批评者指出老子一说暗含操控之术（被术数化的解读）；自由主义一侧则担忧「无人干涉」并不保证「有能力作为」，此正是积极自由与能力路径（森）补上的部分。
bridgeEn: Critics read a hidden statecraft of manipulation into Laozi; on the liberal side the worry is that non-interference does not secure capacity to act—exactly what positive liberty and the capability approach (Sen) were meant to supply.

title: 正名与言语行为
lead: 语言不只是描述世界，还在安置身份与义务——两处抵达同一洞见，问题意识却不同。
leadEn: Language not only describes but installs identities and obligations—two traditions reach the same insight with different questions in view.
west: 奥斯汀与塞尔：以言行事。「我宣布」「我承诺」不报告事实而改变处境，其效力取决于程序、身份与适切条件；制度被理解为言语行为的稳定沉积。
westEn: Austin and Searle: in doing things with words, 'I pronounce' and 'I promise' do not report but alter a situation, their force resting on procedure, status and felicity conditions; institutions are read as sedimented speech acts.
east: 孔子正名以名分规范行为：君君臣臣父父子子——名既是称谓也是职分，违名即失职，故语言的错乱被诊为秩序的错乱。荀子《正名》进一步讨论约定俗成的制名理由。
eastEn: Confucian rectification makes a name a station with duties: ruler, minister, father, son each is what the name obliges; to breach the name is to fail the post, so disorder in language diagnoses disorder in order. Xunzi's Positive Names adds that naming is by convention and for coordination.
bridge: 同一机制（名以立责），两种关切：一个问「意义如何由使用决定」，一个问「秩序如何由名分维系」。合读可同时补齐二者的盲区——语言的社会建构性与制度的规范压力。
bridgeEn: One mechanism (names install obligations), two concerns: how meaning is determined by use, and how order is held by station. Reading them together repairs a blind spot in each—the social construction of language, and the normative pressure of institutions.

sources.label: 奥斯汀《如何以言行事》第二讲
sources.labelEn: Austin, How to Do Things with Words, lect. 2

title: 性恶起伪与自然状态
titleEn: Xunzi's Bad Nature and Hobbes's State of Nature
lead: 从「人不由本性给出秩序」出发，一个通向师礼与教化，一个通向主权与契约。
leadEn: Starting from the thought that order is not given by nature, one road leads to teacher and ritual, the other to sovereign and contract.
west: 霍布斯：自然状态中人人对万物的权利导致战争，理性自保驱使人们让渡权利给绝对主权者；秩序是人为装置，其正当性来自恐惧的解除。
westEn: Hobbes: a right to all things in the state of nature yields war; rational self-preservation drives transfer of right to an absolute sovereign. Order is an artefact justified by the removal of fear.
east: 荀子：性恶（顺情欲则争），故「化性起伪」——礼义与师法作为后天的人为（伪）被圣人所制作，用来分配物质与确立分位；秩序同样人造，但落点在教化与礼的养成而非授权的瞬间。
eastEn: Xunzi: nature is bad—following desire yields contention—so nature must be transformed by conscious activity (wei). Ritual and rightness, made by the sages, allocate goods and fix stations; order is likewise human-made, but the emphasis falls on formation through ritual and teaching, not on a moment of authorisation.
bridge: 关键分歧在「谁制作」与「如何维持」：霍布斯依靠同一主权的强制与承诺的逻辑；荀子依靠经典的学习、师友环境与长期工夫——更接近现代的制度化社会化理论而非契约论。
bridgeEn: The divergence is who makes order and how it is sustained: Hobbes leans on a single sovereign's force and the logic of promise; Xunzi on study of classics, teacher-and-friend environment and long effort—closer to modern theories of institutionalised socialisation than to contract.

sources.label: 霍布斯《利维坦》第十三、十七章

title: 齐物与视角主义
lead: 都否认有无位置的「上帝之眼」，却一个导向安然，一个导向价值的重估。
leadEn: Both deny a view from nowhere; one issues in equanimity, the other in revaluation of values.
west: 尼采：没有事实只有解释，认识是机体需要支配的解释；视角的多元并不取消高下，而以是否增强生命力量来裁判，故须重估一切价值。
westEn: Nietzsche: there are no facts, only interpretations; knowing is interpretation driven by an organism's need to master. A plurality of perspectives does not erase rank, which is judged by enhancement of power—hence the revaluation of all values.
east: 庄子：是非出于「成心」，儒墨各是其所非，辩无胜；以道观之则物无非是，故处理方式是「因是」「寓诸无竟」，让对峙的立场各自安顿。
eastEn: Zhuangzi: right and wrong spring from a fixed mind; Confucians and Mohists each affirm what the other denies, and debate has no winner. Seen from the dao nothing is not so, so the response is to let each side be and rest in the boundless—quieting the standoff rather than ranking it.
bridge: 两者都拒绝把相对主义当作结论，但方向相反：庄子消解的是裁判的必要，尼采争夺的是裁判的资格。前者是心境的改造，后者是价值的战斗。
bridgeEn: Neither accepts relativism as a conclusion, yet in opposite directions: Zhuangzi dissolves the need for a judge, Nietzsche fights over who is entitled to judge. One reformulates temperament, the other wages a war of value.

sources.label: 尼采《善恶的彼岸》前言、残篇 1886–87
sources.labelEn: Nietzsche, Beyond Good and Evil, preface; Nachlass 1886–87

title: 诸蕴无我与知觉束
titleEn: Aggregates and the Bundle of Perceptions
lead: 两个文明在「我」的位置上都只找到过程，却一个用作解脱、一个用作怀疑的界限。
leadEn: Both traditions find only process where a self should be—one draws liberation from it, the other a limit to scepticism.
west: 休谟：向内窥探只抓到某一度量或某种情绪，从未抓到「自我」，故人是知觉的束；但他随即承认，这种同一个人的信念不可消除，只能承认它是想象与习惯的产物。
westEn: Hume: looking inward he catches only this or that perception, never himself, so a person is a bundle; yet he concedes the belief in personal identity cannot be removed—only exposed as the work of imagination and habit.
east: 佛教：五蕴（色受想行识）无常、苦、非我；「我」是于相续上假立之名。分析与解脱在此连成一气——执着有常我为苦之根源，观无我即离执。
eastEn: Buddhism: the five aggregates are impermanent, unsatisfactory and not-self; 'I' is a designation laid over a continuum. Analysis and soteriology are one—grasping at an enduring self is the root of suffering, and seeing non-self releases it.
bridge: 同一去中心化结论，两种实践后果：休谟止步于说明信念如何形成，佛氏据此建立整套禅修与伦理。帕菲特的「这不是一个事实」处在二者之间，说明理论洞见与实践转化之间仍有待解释的差距。
bridgeEn: One decentring conclusion, two practical upshots: Hume stops at explaining how the belief arises, the Buddhist builds meditation and ethics on it. Parfit's 'this is not a further fact' sits between the two, marking still-unexplained distance from insight to practice.

sources.label: 休谟《人性论》第一卷第四篇

title: 中庸与亚里士多德的中道
lead: 都把德性放在过度与不足之间，但对「如何知道中在哪」给出不同的答案。
leadEn: Both place virtue between excess and deficiency, and differ on how one knows where the mean is.
west: 亚里士多德：德性是两个恶之间相对于我们的中道，由实践智慧（phronesis）在具体情形中判定；中道不是算术平均，勇气介于鲁莽与怯懦之间。
westEn: Aristotle: virtue is the mean between two vices, relative to us, determined as the practically wise person would determine it—not an arithmetic average; courage lies between rashness and cowardice.
east: 《中庸》：喜怒哀乐之未发谓之中，发而皆中节谓之和；「中」含本体（未发之中）与工夫（时中）两层，须以慎独与涵养在事上校准。
eastEn: The Doctrine of the Mean: equilibrium before the rise of feeling is zhong; feeling rising in due measure is harmony. Zhong carries both an ontological layer (unaroused centrality) and a task-layer (timely centrality), calibrated through vigilance over the unseen and nourishment in affairs.
bridge: 结构惊人的相似，重心却不同：希腊侧把中道交给有判断力的行动者，儒侧把中道接上宇宙论（致中和，天地位焉，万物育焉）。因此一边通向德性伦理学，一边通向修养论与秩序论的一体化表述。
bridgeEn: The structures are strikingly alike, the centres of gravity not: Greece hands the mean to a judging agent, Confucianism reconnects it to cosmology—reach equilibrium and harmony and heaven and earth keep their places. Hence one side issues in virtue ethics, the other in a unified account of cultivation and order.

sources.label: 亚里士多德《尼各马可伦理学》第二卷

title: 致良知与道德自律
lead: 王阳明说善恶不待外求、当下一念即是良知；康德说道德律出自自由意志的自我立法。二者都把道德之根扎进「心」而非外在权威。
leadEn: Wang Yangming holds good and evil need no outer search—the present thought is innate knowing; Kant holds the moral law is self-legislation of a free will. Both root morality in the 'mind', not in outer authority.
west: 康德以定言命令立则：只按你愿意其成为普遍法则的准则去行动；道德价值出于义务而非偏好，理性为自己立法即是自律与人之尊严的根源。
westEn: Kant's categorical imperative: act only on a maxim you could will as universal law; moral worth comes from duty not inclination, and reason's self-legislation is the root of autonomy and human dignity.
east: 阳明提出「无善无恶心之体，有善有恶意之动……知善知恶是良知」：良知人人本具、不假外求，将其在事上磨炼扩充即成德，权威在内而不在经典教条。
eastEn: Yangming: 'the body of mind is beyond good and evil... to know good and evil is innate knowing'—liangzhi is complete in everyone and sought outward in nothing; extending and tempering it through affairs is virtue, with authority within rather than in texts.
bridge: 两者都以内在立法对抗他律，却一重普遍形式的理性检验，一重当下直觉的扩充践履；良知能否经得起康德的普遍化测试，正是这场对话的张力所在。
bridgeEn: Both answer heteronomy with inner lawgiving, yet one stresses universal rational form, the other the extension of present intuition—whether liangzhi can pass Kant's test of universalisation is the live tension of the dialogue.

sources.label: 王阳明《传习录》
sources.labelEn: Wang Yangming, Instructions for Practical Living

sources.label: 康德《道德形而上学奠基》
sources.labelEn: Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals

title: 易之变与万物流变
titleEn: The Book of Changes and Panta Rhei
lead: 「生生之谓易」与「人不能两次踏入同一条河流」：两种文明都以变易为世界的底色，却各自给出了不同的落点。
leadEn: 'Ceaseless birth-and-rebirth is the Change' and 'you cannot step twice into the same river': two cultures both take flux as the world's keynote, yet land it differently.
west: 赫拉克利特以逻各斯统摄对立与流变、以火为本原；但巴门尼德—柏拉图一线判定流变属意见、真实者恒常不动，西方遂长期押注于「变中之常」。
westEn: Heraclitus rules flux and opposition by the logos, with fire as principle; but the Parmenides–Plato line assigns flux to opinion and being to the unchanging, so the West long bet on permanence behind change.
east: 《易》以阴阳消息、刚柔相推写尽变易，却不在变化背后另立不变实体；「时中」教人在流转中随时取中、顺势而成，恒常只安于变化本身。
eastEn: The Yijing charts change through the waxing and waning of yin and yang yet posits no unchanging substance behind it; 'timely equilibrium' teaches one to hit the mean within flux—constancy residing in change itself.
bridge: 同以流变为实在，一侧逼出「现象／本体」的二分，一侧走向「即用见体、唯变所适」；这一分岔几乎决定了西方形而上学与《易》学气质之别。
bridgeEn: Both grant flux reality, yet one forces the appearance/being split while the other seeks 'substance seen in function, at home only in change'—a fork that all but decides the difference between Western metaphysics and the temper of Yijing thought.

title: 禅门公案与哲学的治疗
lead: 临济的「吃茶去」、赵州的「狗子无佛性」，与维特根斯坦「给苍蝇指出飞出捕蝇瓶的路」——都以搅乱语言来解结，而非另立新论。
leadEn: Linji's 'go and drink tea', Zhaozhou's 'dog—no buddha-nature', and Wittgenstein's 'show the fly the way out of the fly-bottle' all untie by jumbling language, not by founding a new thesis.
west: 后期维特根斯坦把哲学问题视为语言误用所致的「智力痉挛」，其方法不是解答而是消解：把词交回日常用法，让人看清语法的迷宫而获得安宁。
westEn: The later Wittgenstein treats philosophical problems as a 'cramp of the mind' bred by misusing language; his method dissolves rather than answers, returning words to everyday use until one sees the grammar-maze and finds peace.
east: 禅宗自居「不立文字、教外别传」，却大量借公案、机锋、棒喝逼学人放下对概念的执取、直指见性；语言在此被用来打破语言自身的惯性。
eastEn: Chán professes a transmission outside the letters, yet leans heavily on kōan, sharp exchange and shock to press the student to drop conceptual grasp and see directly; language here is the tool used to break language's own inertia.
bridge: 两者都不建体系而从事「治疗」，分歧却在有没有「治疗之后」的境界：维氏归于用法之平宁，禅者指向不可言说的开悟。
bridgeEn: Both build no system and practise 'therapy', yet divide on whether there is any state 'after therapy': Wittgenstein settles into the peace of use, the Chan pointer toward an unsayable awakening.

sources.label: 《无门关》《碧岩录》公案集
sources.labelEn: The Gateless Barrier / Blue Cliff Record

title: 格物致知与本质直观
lead: 朱熹要「即物而穷其理」，胡塞尔要「回到事情本身、直观其本质」：二者都把认知落点放在事物之自身显现，而非主观臆断。
leadEn: Zhu Xi would 'exhaust principle through things', Husserl 'return to the things themselves and intuit their essence': both anchor knowing in a thing's self-showing, not subjective guesswork.
west: 胡塞尔以现象学还原（悬置自然态度）剥离成见，让本质在直观中当场呈现；再以「自由想象变更」变换诸例，把其中不变的结构照面出来。
westEn: Husserl's phenomenological reduction brackets the natural attitude so essences show themselves in intuition; 'free imaginative variation' then varies examples to bring out the invariant structure within them.
east: 朱熹的「格物致知」主张即一草一木、一事一物而穷其理，积习既久终能豁然贯通；阳明则反转其义，谓「格」者「正」也，理不在物而在心之良知。
eastEn: Zhu Xi's 'investigate things to extend knowledge' reads principle in every plant and affair until, long practised, it breaks through at a glance; Yangming reverses it—'investigate' means 'rectify', and principle lies not in things but in the mind's innate knowing.
bridge: 两者都重「让事物如其所是地被给予」，但一以直观把握超时间的本质，一以格物贯通伦理的天理；阳明式的转向更逼问：穷理究竟当向外，还是向内？
bridgeEn: Both prize 'letting the thing be given just as it is', yet one intuits a timeless essence and the other threads an ethical principle through things; Yangming's turn presses the further question—does exhausting principle go outward, or inward?

title: 墨家辩经与三段论
lead: 墨家率先写下辩论的规矩，亚里士多德把推理几何化；一个成了论辩工具，一个成了形式学科。
leadEn: Mohists first wrote rules of disputation; Aristotle geometrized inference—one stayed an argument tool, the other became a formal discipline.
west: 《前分析篇》从论证中抽离纯形式：三个词项、两个前提必然推出结论，格与式可脱离内容单独检验。逻辑由此成为可授受的科目——斯多亚与中世纪经院把它纳入课程底座，直到 19 世纪数学逻辑重启其叙事。
westEn: The Prior Analytics abstracts pure form from argument: three terms and two premises necessitate a conclusion, figure and mood testable apart from content. Logic becomes a teachable subject—Stoics and medieval schools set it as curriculum bedrock until 19th-century mathematical logic reopened its story.
east: 墨子以「三表」为立论立据：有本之于古者、有原察百姓耳目之实者、有用之刑政观其中国家百姓之利者。后期墨家《小取》细密到「辟、侔、援、推」四式与诸过犯，但正确性的最终判准仍落在「是否迁国家百姓之利」——形式与内容从未彻底剥离，演绎的张力没有自立为一门学科。
eastEn: Mozi's three gauges license argument: grounded in the ancient, verified against common ears and eyes, applied in governance to weigh the people's benefit. The later Mohist Xiao Qu refines analogy, parallel, citation and extension with catalogued fallacies—yet the final test stays consequentialist: form never fully detaches from content, and the deductive tension never spun off into an autonomous discipline.
bridge: 比较的不是谁更聪明，而是制度与激励：希腊的法庭与城邦辩论让「有效式」成为可售卖的技艺，战国的百家争鸣让「言之效」成为终极裁判；同一路推法，一支走向三段论，一支走向判例式类推。名实之辩（见「名实之辩与共相之争」条）管本体论，本条管推理技艺为何在一边成学科、在另一边不成。
bridgeEn: Not who was smarter, but institutions and incentives: Greek courts and civic debate made valid form a sellable skill; the Warring States contest of schools made efficacy of speech the final judge. Down one path the same inference became syllogistics; down the other, case-like analogy. The universals entry handles ontology; this one handles why the art of reason became a discipline on one side and not the other.

title: 礼治秩序与法治秩序
lead: 一端靠角色与习俗的养成，一端靠成文规则的颁布与强制——儒家法家在中国内部吵完，希腊人早就在城邦里辩过一轮。
leadEn: One order rests on trained roles and custom, the other on promulgated rules and enforcement—Confucians and Legalists fought it inside China; the Greeks had debated it in the polis first.
west: 从梭伦立法到亚里士多德「法治优于一人之治」，人为法成为被正面反思的对象；斯多亚的普遍之法落入罗马法学，经中世纪教会法与近代社会契约论，长成「法律之下人人平等」的宪政语法的底座。
westEn: From Solon's statutes to Aristotle's 'rule of law over rule of any man', positive law becomes a reflected object; the Stoic universal law descends into Roman jurisprudence, through medieval canon law and early-modern contract theory, into the grammar of constitutional equality under law.
east: 孔子答为政：「道之以政，齐之以刑，民免而无耻；道之以德，齐之以礼，有耻且格。」礼不只是仪节，而是分角色、分器物、分资源的秩序图；法家则有相当完整的成文法体系与「刑无等级」的执行。秦以法得天下、汉以后以「德礼为政教之本，刑罚为政教之用」（《唐律疏议》序）合流——礼与法对峙又互济，争的是法律本身还需不需要一个更上的正当性来源。
eastEn: Confucius on governance: lead by decrees and align by punishments, people dodge without shame; lead by virtue and align by ritual, people gain shame and correct themselves. Li is not mere ceremony but a map allocating roles, things and resources; the Legalists fielded near-complete written codes with punishment above rank. Qin took the realm by law; since Han the two merged—'virtue and ritual the root of governance, punishment its instrument' (preface to the Tang Code). The fight was whether law itself needs a higher source of legitimacy.
bridge: 真实分歧不在「有没有法」——法家有完整的制定法；而在法的位阶：希腊—罗马传统让法接受正义与自然的外在评判，中国传统让法在礼与人情之内履职。今天「法治与德治相结合」的表述，仍是这场两千年辩论的最新一层。与「天理与自然法」条分工：那条讲超越根据，本条讲秩序技术。
bridgeEn: The split is not whether laws existed—the Legalists had full statutes—but their rank: the Greek-Roman line lets law be judged by an external justice and nature; the Chinese line lets law serve inside ritual and human feeling. Today's 'combining rule of law with rule of virtue' is the newest layer of a 2,000-year quarrel. Against the heaven-principle/natural-law entry: that one covers transcendental grounding; this one covers the technology of order.

title: 内圣外王与哲学王
titleEn: Sage Within, King Without vs. Philosopher-King
lead: 谁配统治？儒家给出道德楷模，柏拉图给出见过「善」的人；一个靠修身向外推，一个靠辩证法而上。
leadEn: Who deserves to rule? Confucianism offers the moral exemplar, Plato one who has seen the Good—one extends self-cultivation outward, the other ascends by dialectic.
west: 《理想国》的城邦里，唯有走出洞穴、见过善之理念者堪当大任：童年练音乐与体操，三十岁起学算术几何诸科预备，五十岁方「下去」执掌城邦——统治不是选举的产物，而是被真理转身之后的义务。
westEn: In the Republic only those who leave the cave and see the Form of the Good are fit to rule: music and gymnastics in childhood, the mathematical propaedeutic from thirty, and only at fifty do they 'go down' to govern—rule is not elected but an obligation incurred after being turned toward truth.
east: 「内圣外王」（《庄子·天下》）与《中庸》「虽有其位，苟无其德，不敢作礼乐焉；虽有其德，苟无其位，亦不敢作礼乐焉」把统治资格同时挂德与位上；现实等不来圣人，替代机制是「选贤与能」的荐举与科举——政治正当性连到学问与道德示范，君主本人须先经经筵与史官的双重规训。
eastEn: 'Sage within, king without' (Zhuangzi, Under Heaven) and the Doctrine of the Mean's twin clause—no rites or music composed without both the position and the virtue—hang legitimacy on moral worth and seat together. Sages never arrive on schedule, so recommendation and the examination state substituted: legitimacy ties to learning and exemplarity, the emperor himself disciplined first by classical readings and the historians' brush.
bridge: 两套方案都在回应「权力应交给智慧」的焦虑，验收方向却相反：柏拉图是事前考试制（谁见过善），儒家是事后史观制（治下之民是否有耻且格）。现代政治哲学的认识论民主之争（专家治理 vs 民意授权）仍在这两个坐标之间摆动。
bridgeEn: Both answer the anxiety that power should be entrusted to wisdom, with opposite acceptance tests: Plato's is an ante-mortem examination (who has seen the Good), Confucianism's a post-mortem historiography (did the people gain shame and rectitude). Today's epistemic-democracy quarrel—technocracy vs. mandate of the people—still swings between these coordinates.

title: 蝶梦与恶魔假设
titleEn: Butterfly Dream vs. the Evil Demon
lead: 一个在人与蝶之间醒来，一个把怀疑住到「我思」为止——同设一个现实全面崩塌的场景，找回的路径正好相反。
leadEn: One wakes between man and butterfly; the other dwells in doubt until 'I think'—the same collapse of reality, opposite recoveries.
west: 笛卡尔的方法论怀疑在《第一哲学沉思集》里剥掉感觉、醒觉乃至算术，假设一个全能恶魔使一切为假，只为找一块不可疑的阿基米德点：「我思故我在」从残渣中立起，再用清楚明白的观念、上帝之存在把外部世界重新拼装回来——判准放在无可怀疑的主体。
westEn: Descartes' methodical doubt strips sensation, wakefulness even arithmetic, housing an omnipotent evil demon to make all false—all to find one Archimedean point: 'I think, I am' rises from the residue, and clear and distinct ideas, God's veracity, reassemble the world—certainty lodged in the indubitable subject.
east: 庄周梦蝶「栩栩然胡蝶也，自喻适志与」，觉后「则周也」——故事不停在「哪个是真的」，而落在「周与胡蝶，则必有分矣——此之谓物化」：怀疑不是索取确定性的梯子，而是物与物互化的观照；判准被化掉而不是被修复。与「庄周梦蝶」思想实验条分工：那条展开实验本身，本条对照两种文明的找回方式。
eastEn: Zhuang Zhou 'blissful as a butterfly, content with his own way'; waking, 'then he was Zhou'—the tale does not stop at which was real but lands on the passing over of things into each other: doubt is not a ladder demanding certainty but an apprehension of transformation—the criterion dissolved rather than repaired. Against the standalone butterfly-dream experiment: that one unpacks the puzzle; this one contrasts how two cultures recover.
bridge: 「你怎么知道没在做梦」在近代认识论里以「经验不可决定论」与「缸中之脑」重演，两边文本仍可各读一半：笛卡尔一系把怀疑当知识地基的破损待修，庄子一系把怀疑当观点的轮转可安。把「醒来」本身当作需要解释的概念，是两边共同留给今天的作业。
bridgeEn: The dream question returns as underdetermination of experience and the brain-in-a-vat; both texts still supply half the answer: the Cartesian line treats doubt as damage to knowledge's foundation awaiting repair, the Zhuangzian line as rotation of vantage to be settled into. Treating 'waking up' itself as the concept needing gloss is the homework both leave us.
